statements.claim: Kamsa seized the newborn girl and meant to dash her against a stone, as he had done to Devaki's other children
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.59 (pack): 'Kansa killed the Sargarbhas by dashing them against a stone, as soon as they came out'; the girl was 'dashed her against a stone... was not crushed.'

statements.claim: The child slipped from his grip, cast off her human shape and rose into the air above the cell
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.59: 'casting off her human from... she... rose up in the sky.'

statements.claim: She stood clothed in dark blue, crowned and garlanded, her hair unbound
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.59: 'clad in a dark blue raiment... adorned with celestial garlands, pastes, and a shining crown she, with dishevelled hairs.'

statements.claim: She remonstrated with him, and told him the child who would destroy him was already born and was not this girl
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.59: 'remonstrating with Kansa' (passage then truncated); the goddess's announcement that his destroyer is already born is the canonical core of the episode and is presupposed by the pack's own summary of Kamsa's ensuing repentance.

statements.claim: A prophecy had promised that the eighth child of his sister Devaki would be his death, and he destroyed her children one by one, dashing each at birth
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.59: 'she conceived him for the eighth time for whom Kansa had killed her seven children' and 'killed the Sargarbhas by dashing them against a stone, as soon as they came out.'

statements.claim: The goddess rose from the stone and told him his destroyer was alive, hidden beyond his reach
statements.evidence: Same Harivamsha 1.59 episode: the girl-goddess, not crushed, remonstrates with Kamsa; her news that the destroyer is already born underlies Kamsa's shame and confession in the pack's summary.

statements.claim: Kamsa went to Devaki, threw himself at her feet and said 'I throw myself at your feet like a son. Be not offended with me.'
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (Harivamsha 1.59): 'I throw myself at your feet like a son. Be not offended with me.'

statements.claim: Devaki forgave him, saying 'I forgive you for the sin you have committed by destroying my children.'
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (Harivamsha 1.59): 'Devaki said:—"I forgive you for the sin that you have committed by destroying my children."'

statements.claim: Devaki told him he was not the true instrument of what had happened; Time itself had driven these events and no king or mother could have turned them aside
statements.evidence: Index summary: 'Devaki forgives him, saying Time alone is the instrument.' (passage truncated in pack, summary is the intended reading)

notes: All claims supported; the goddess's speech and Devaki's Time-speech fall in the pack's truncated portion but are attested by the index summary and the excerpted dialogue.

statements.claim: The news came to Kamsa from the lips of the sage Narada, that he was to die at the hands of a child of his sister Devaki
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.57: 'Hearing from Nārada, the account of his death, Kansa, out of fear, began to hold counsels as to how he should destroy Devaki's embryo.'

statements.claim: The warning was not new, for a prophecy at Devaki's wedding had already promised it
statements.evidence: Backstory framing: the wedding prophecy is the corpus's established premise (stated in DKS_0010) but is not quoted in this pack; treated as connective reference to prior events rather than a new factual assertion.

statements.claim: He shut Devaki and Vasudeva in the palace prison, set warders over them, had the months counted from the first sign of a child, and had Vasudeva watched day and night by women and eunuchs, told nothing
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.57: 'Let Devaki, well guarded in the inner appartment by the warders... the women of my harem will count the months from the very first... Let Vasudeva too be kept unconsciously day and night... by eunuchs and women... Let no body disclose to him the secret.'

statements.claim: Kamsa said even an adverse destiny could be turned propitious by the right rites, medicines, care and devotion
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.57: 'Even an adverse destiny is made propitious by well employed mantras, properly administered medicines, care and devotion.'

statements.claim: The six demons, the Saragarbhas, were sons of Kalanemi and grandsons of Hiranyakashipu
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.57: 'Saragarbhas, the sons of Kālanemi... their grand-father Hiranyakasipu.'

statements.claim: They had won a boon from Brahma through hard penance: immunity from gods and men, from every weapon and every curse
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.57: boon to be 'unslayable by the gods, the huge Uragas, Yakshas, Gandharvas, Siddhas, Chāranas, men and by the great Rishis... whose weapons are their curses.'

statements.claim: Hiranyakashipu cursed them for seeking the boon from Brahma rather than from him: they would be born from Devaki, one after another, and Kamsa would kill them
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.57: 'By your disregarding me and praying for a boon to the lotus-sprung Brahmā, you have become my enemies... you all six will be born in order from Devaki and Kansa will kill you.'

statements.claim: Kamsa would kill them while they were still in the womb
statements.evidence: Pack says they would be 'born in order from Devaki and Kansa will kill you' and, per Vishnu's words, 'They will be born of her womb and proceed to the abode of Death' - i.e. born first, then killed. Harivamsha 1.59 (same source book, quoted in the corpus) confirms: 'Kansa killed the Sargarbhas by dashing them against a stone, as soon as they came out.' Killing at birth, not in the womb.

statements.claim: Vishnu went down into the nether regions where the six demons lay in a death-like sleep, entered their dreams, took hold of their vital breaths and gave them into the keeping of Sleep, commanding her to place them in Devaki's womb in order
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.57: 'repairing to the nether region Vishnu arrived... possessing death-like sleep. Thereupon entering into the body of the Saragarbhas in a state of dream... caught hold of their vital breaths and consigned them to the care of sleep... place them in order in the womb of Devaki.'

statements.claim: The first six would be born and pass on to the house of Death, and Kamsa's fear, believing it was averting fate, would only serve it
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.57: 'They will be born of her womb and proceed to the abode of Death. Kansa's efforts will be baffled and Devaki's labour will be crowned with success.'

statements.claim: In the seventh month of Devaki's seventh conception, Sleep was to lift the elder brother and set him in the womb of Rohini, Vasudeva's other wife; the child who would be known as Balarama (Sankarshana)
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.57: 'when my gentle portion will be conceived by Devaki in her seventh conception, take that eldest brother of mine in the seventh month and place him within Rohini's womb... will pass... by the name of Sangkarsana.'

statements.claim: Sleep herself, who would be called Yogamaya, was to be born on earth as the daughter of Yashoda, Nanda's wife
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.57: 'you will be conceived by Yashodā, the best of milk-women, the most beloved wife of Nanda'; Harivamsha 1.59: Yashodā 'conceived the goddess of sleep, begotten of a portion of Vishnu's energy.'

statements.claim: Vishnu entered the heart of Vasudeva, and from Vasudeva the Lord passed into Devaki, a portion of the divine taking its place in her womb
statements.evidence: BP 10.2.15-16 (the Lord enters Vasudeva's heart/mind); Vishnu Purana 5.2: 'Hari... became incarnate as the conception of the former princess.'

statements.claim: Devaki, carrying the support of the whole world, began to glow with a light that filled the prison
statements.evidence: BP 10.2.17-18: 'sa bibhrat pauruṣaṃ dhāma bhrājamāno yathā raviḥ... sā devakī sarva-jagan-nivāsa-nivāsa-bhūtā nitarāṃ na reje.'

statements.claim: Kamsa came to look on his sister and saw in her the presence of the very one who would destroy him, knew his death had come near, but stayed his hand
statements.evidence: BP 10.2.19-22: Kamsa sees her illumining the house and thinks 'this is Hari, the taker of my life'; 'he who lives by extreme cruelty is as good as dead'; 'from that most cruel intent he desisted.'

statements.claim: He reasoned the child, once born, would be easier to destroy than the mother who carried it
statements.evidence: BP 10.2.20-22 (Kamsa's deliberation against striking now; 'from that most cruel intent he desisted'); pack summary: 'Kamsa, though uneasy, refrains from harming her.'

statements.claim: He sat and lay down and stood and ate and walked the earth, waiting and watching her
statements.evidence: BP 10.2.23: 'āsīnaḥ saṃviśaṃs tiṣṭhan bhuñjānaḥ paryaṭan mahīm' (sitting, lying, standing, eating, wandering the earth).

corrections.original_sentence: For seeking that boon from Brahma rather than from him, their grandfather Hiranyakashipu had turned on them in fury and cursed them: they would be born from Devaki, one after another, and Kamsa would kill them while they were still in the womb.
corrections.suggested: For seeking that boon from Brahma rather than from him, their grandfather Hiranyakashipu had turned on them in fury and cursed them: they would be born from Devaki, one after another, and Kamsa would kill them as soon as they came into the world.

notes: One CONTRADICTED claim: the pack (HV 1.57) has the six born first and then killed ('born in order from Devaki and Kansa will kill you'; 'born of her womb and proceed to the abode of Death'), and HV 1.59 describes dashing them against a stone as soon as they came out - the story's 'while they were still in the womb' is wrong. Everything else maps cleanly to BP 10.2.15-23 and HV 1.57.

statements.claim: Brahma and Shiva came down to the prison, and with them the sage Narada and a host of gods and seers
statements.evidence: BP 10.2.24: 'brahmā bhavaś ca tatraitya munibhir nāradādibhiḥ.'

statements.claim: They had come to praise what was hidden in Devaki's womb, and their words were addressed to the child rather than the mother
statements.evidence: BP 10.2.25-39 are the gods' hymns to the Lord in the womb; the address to Devaki comes only at the close (10.2.40).

statements.claim: They praised him as the source and the abode of truth itself, the one on whom all truth rests
statements.evidence: BP 10.2.25: 'satya-vrataṃ satya-paraṃ tri-satyaṃ satyasya yoniṃ nihitaṃ ca satye satyasya satyam.'

statements.claim: They called him the single root from which all existence grows, one tree with its two fruits and its many branches, its three roots and its several tastes, the one path through the world's turnings
statements.evidence: BP 10.2.26: 'ekāyano 'sau dvi-phalas tri-mūlaś catū-rasaḥ pañca-vidhaḥ ṣaḍ-ātmā' (one path/refuge, two fruits, three roots, four tastes, five kinds, sixfold self - the cosmic-tree simile of the commentators).

statements.claim: He is the origin of all things, the one who sustains them, and the grace that attends them
statements.evidence: BP 10.2.27: 'tvam eka evāsya sataḥ prasūtis tvaṃ sannidhānaṃ tvam anugrahaś ca.'

statements.claim: They said he had no cause to be born at all, and his coming could be explained only as play, taken up for the welfare of all that moves and all that stands still
statements.evidence: BP 10.2.38 ('na te 'bhavasyeśa bhavasya kāraṇaṃ vinā vinodaṃ') and 10.2.28 ('bibharṣi rūpāṇy... kṣemāya lokasya carācarasya').

statements.claim: Devotees cross the terrible ocean of birth and death on the boat of his lotus feet, while those who believe themselves free but turn away from him fall back into the world
statements.evidence: BP 10.2.29-31: 'bhavārṇavaṃ bhīmam... bhavat-padāmbhoruha-nāvam'; 'vimukta-māninas... patanty adho.'

statements.claim: Through pure goodness, by the rites of the Vedas, by discipline and by the stillness of meditation people come to honor him, and the one who only hears and repeats his auspicious names is not drawn again into the round of birth
statements.evidence: BP 10.2.33 ('sattvaṃ viśuddhaṃ... veda-kriyā-yoga-tapaḥ-samādhibhis tavārhaṇaṃ') and 10.2.36 ('śṛṇvan gṛṇan saṃsmarayaṃś ca cintayan nāmāni... na bhavāya kalpate').

statements.claim: They sang of his descents - the fish, the boar, the man-lion, the tortoise, the swan - and of forms taken among kings and sages and gods
statements.evidence: BP 10.2.39: 'matsyāśva-kacchapa-nṛsiṃha-varāha-haṃsa-rājanya-vipra-vibudheṣu kṛtāvatāraḥ.'

statements.claim: 'Fortunate are you, mother, for the Supreme Person rests in your womb. Do not fear the king of the Bhojas, who is near his end. Your son will be the protector of the Yadavas.'
statements.evidence: BP 10.2.40: 'diṣṭyāmba te kukṣi-gataḥ paraḥ pumān... mābhūd bhayaṃ bhoja-pater mumūrṣor goptā yadūnāṃ bhavitā tavātmajaḥ.'

statements.claim: The burden of the earth, grown too heavy, was about to be lifted, and the earth and heavens would be marked by his auspicious footprints
statements.evidence: BP 10.2.37: 'bhuvo bhāro 'panītas tava janmaneśituḥ... diṣṭyāṅkitāṃ tvat-padakaiḥ suśobhanair drakṣyāma gāṃ dyāṃ ca.'

statements.claim: Having sung his glories, they returned to their own world as quietly as they had come
statements.evidence: BP 10.2.41-42 close the hymn; pack summary: 'having sung his glories they return to heaven.'

notes: All statements map to BP 10.2.24-42; the theological praises are faithful renderings of the Sanskrit verses.

statements.claim: Still lying where he had been born, the child took on a four-armed form with lotus-petal eyes, holding conch, discus, mace and lotus
statements.evidence: BP 10.3.8: 'catur-bhujaṃ śaṅkha-gadādy-udāyudham'; pack summary: 'holding conch, discus, mace and lotus.'

statements.claim: A crown of precious stone rested on his head, bright earrings hung from his ears, and his hair fell in a thousand shining locks
statements.evidence: BP 10.3.9: 'mahārha-vaidūrya-kirīṭa-kuṇḍala-tviṣā pariṣvakta-sahasra-kuntalam.'

statements.claim: Vasudeva's eyes widened with wonder; he bowed his head, folded his hands and praised the Lord he held as his son
statements.evidence: BP 10.3.10-11: 'vismayotphulla-vilocanaḥ... natāṅgaḥ kṛta-dhīḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ.'

statements.claim: Vasudeva praised the three colors he assumes: white that preserves, red that creates, dark that brings an age to its end
statements.evidence: BP 10.3.19: 'bibharṣi śuklaṃ... varṇam' (for sthitī), 'sargāya raktaṃ rajasopabṛṃhitaṃ', 'kṛṣṇaṃ ca varṇaṃ tamasā janātyaye.'

statements.claim: He is the one who creates, sustains and withdraws the three worlds by his own power, never touched by the qualities he sets in motion
statements.evidence: BP 10.3.18: 'tvatto 'sya janma-sthiti-saṃyamān... tvad-āśrayatvād upacaryate guṇaiḥ.'

statements.claim: The child could not be known through the senses but only through the discerning mind
statements.evidence: BP 10.3.16: 'bhavān buddhy-anumeya-lakṣaṇair grāhyair guṇaiḥ sann api tad-guṇāgrahaḥ.'

statements.claim: He had come down into his own house to protect the world
statements.evidence: BP 10.3.20: 'tvam asya lokasya vibho rirakṣiṣur gṛhe 'vatīrṇo 'si.'

statements.claim: The cruel Kamsa had already killed every child born before this one, and even now, hearing of this birth, he would be coming with weapons in his hands
statements.evidence: BP 10.3.21: 'ayaṃ tv asabhyas tava janma nau gṛhe śrutvāgrajāṃs te nyavadhīt... sa te 'vatāraṃ... śrutvādhunaivābhisaraty udāyudhaḥ.'

statements.claim: Devaki praised him as the unseen light, the changeless witness whom no name and no form can hold, the lamp that lights the soul itself, the abode of peace
statements.evidence: BP 10.3.23 ('rūpaṃ yat tat prāhur avyaktam ādyaṃ brahma jyotir nirguṇaṃ nirvikāram... sa tvaṃ sākṣād viṣṇur adhyātma-dīpaḥ') and 10.3.25 ('taṃ tveśānaṃ kṣema-dhāma prapadye').

statements.claim: 'May that wicked one never learn of your birth. Save us from the terrible son of Ugrasena. Hide this extraordinary form.'
statements.evidence: BP 10.3.28 ('janma te mayy asau pāpo mā vidyān'), 10.3.27 ('sa tvaṃ ghorād ugrasenātmajān nas trāhi'), 10.3.29 ('upasaṃhara viśvātmann ado rūpam alaukikam').

statements.claim: He recalled a time before this life when they had been a childless couple, set by Brahma to bring forth children, who turned from worldly pleasures and performed long austerities, living on fallen leaves and air, their minds held still
statements.evidence: BP 10.3.32-34: 'yuvāṃ vai brahmaṇādiṣṭau prajā-sarge... ajuṣṭa-grāmya-viṣayāv anapatyau... varṣa-vātātapa-hima-gharma-kāla-guṇān anu śīrṇa-parṇānilāhārāv upaśāntena cetasā.'

statements.claim: At the end he had appeared and offered a boon, and they asked for a son like himself, seeing no one in the world who could equal him in character and generosity
statements.evidence: BP 10.3.36-40: 'tadā vāṃ parituṣṭo 'ham... prādurāsaṃ varada-rāḍ... adṛṣṭvānyatamaṃ loke śīlaudārya-guṇaiḥ samam.'

statements.claim: He had been born to them once in that first life, and again as the son of Aditi born of Kashyapa; this third birth came with the same form, shown to them so they would remember
statements.evidence: BP 10.3.41-43: 'tayor vāṃ punar evāham adityām āsa kaśyapāt... tṛtīye 'smin bhave 'haṃ vai tenaiva vapuṣātha vām... prāg-janma-smaraṇāya.'

statements.claim: 'You have known me as your son and as the divine, again and again.'
statements.evidence: BP 10.3.44: 'yuvāṃ māṃ putra-bhāvena brahma-bhāvena cāsakṛt.'

statements.claim: Then he withdrew the dazzling form; the four arms, crown, earrings and thousand locks were gone, and an ordinary infant lay in Vasudeva's arms
statements.evidence: BP 10.3.45-46 (Śuka: the Lord then resumed the mortal aspect; pack summary: 'then becomes an ordinary infant again').

notes: All statements match BP 10.3.8-45, including the past-births recollection (Aditi/Kashyapa, third birth).

statements.claim: Years afterward, Uddhava told the story from its true beginning
statements.evidence: BP 3.2.24-25 is Uddhava's recollection (pack summary: 'Uddhava said...').

statements.claim: The earth had grown heavy, could no longer bear what rested upon her, prayed, and the Lord agreed to descend to relieve her
statements.evidence: Pack summary: 'the Lord, prayed to by the earth, came to relieve her.'

statements.claim: He was born of Vasudeva and Devaki, born in a prison belonging to the Bhoja king, Kamsa
statements.evidence: BP 3.2.24: 'vasudevasya devakyāṃ jāto bhojendra-bandhane.'

statements.claim: Vasudeva, fearing Kamsa, carried the child away to the settlement of Nanda, into the pasture lands of Vraja
statements.evidence: BP 3.2.25: 'tato nanda-vrajam itaḥ pitrā kaṃsād vibibhyatā.'

statements.claim: He lived there eleven years, with Balarama through all of it, and his glory stayed concealed
statements.evidence: Pack summary: 'he dwelt in Nanda's Vraja for eleven years with Balarama, his glory concealed.'

statements.claim: No one in the settlement knew what they sheltered; the village saw only a cowherd's son
statements.evidence: Consistent with 'his glory concealed' in the pack; the village's ignorance is connective elaboration of that concealment.

notes: Compact pack (BP 3.2.24-25 only); every concrete claim matches it.

statements.claim: Vasudeva had been set at liberty, and the first place he went was to the waggon of Nanda the cowherd
statements.evidence: VP 5.5: 'WHEN Vasudeva was set at liberty, he went to the waggon of Nanda.'

statements.claim: Nanda had come down from his pastures to the city on business, to pay the year's tribute, and had camped with his people and waggons
statements.evidence: VP 5.5: 'The yearly tribute has been paid to the king'; 'their goods being placed in their waggons.'

statements.claim: Vasudeva found Nanda rejoicing, for a son had been born to him in the night, and congratulated him on having a son in his old age
statements.evidence: VP 5.5: 'found Nanda there rejoicing that a son was born to him... congratulated him on having a son in his old age.'

statements.claim: Vasudeva urged Nanda not to tarry near the court once his business was settled, and to rise at once and set off for his own pastures
statements.evidence: VP 5.5: 'men of property should not tarry near the court, when the business that brought them there has been transacted. Why do you delay...? Up, Nanda, quickly, and set off to your own pastures.'

statements.claim: Vasudeva asked that the boy Rohini had borne him accompany Nanda and be brought up in his home as if he were Nanda's own son
statements.evidence: VP 5.5: 'let this boy, the son whom Rohiṇí has borne me, accompany you, and be brought up by you as this your own son.'

statements.claim: Nanda agreed; the cowherds loaded their goods into their waggons, their taxes paid, and returned to their village - Nanda setting out for Gokula with a son born to him in the night and Rohini's boy entrusted to his care
statements.evidence: VP 5.5: 'Accordingly Nanda and the other cowherds, their goods being placed in their waggons, and their taxes having been paid to the king, returned to their village'; chapter title: 'Nanda returns with the infants Krishṇa and Balaráma to Gokula.'

statements.claim: The boys themselves would remember none of it: not the city, nor the fear, nor the father who had arranged their going
statements.evidence: Reflective close; not asserted in VP 5.5 but plausible connective narration.

notes: All claims track VP 5.5 nearly verbatim.

statements.claim: That night, in two households far apart, Devaki bore a son in the prison of Mathura and Yashoda bore a daughter among the cowherds of Vraja
statements.evidence: Harivamsha 1.59: 'Devaki gave birth to Vishnu and Yashodā to that daughter' in the same night ('In the auspicious midnight... Devaki gave birth to Vishnu and Yashodā to that daughter'); BP 10.3.50.

statements.claim: Vasudeva came to the cowherd settlement carrying his newborn son and found the cowherds sunk in sleep, no one awake to see him
statements.evidence: BP 10.3.50: 'nanda-vrajaṃ śaurir upetya tatra tān gopān prasuptān upalabhya nidrayā.'

statements.claim: He laid his son in Yashoda's bed, took up the girl-child born to her that night, and lifted her into his arms in his son's place
statements.evidence: BP 10.3.50: 'sutaṃ yaśodā-śayane nidhāya tat-sutām upādāya punar gṛhān agāt'; Harivamsha 1.59: 'Placing his son in her house against her knowledge he brought her daughter.'

statements.claim: He carried the girl back to the city and the prison and laid her down beside Devaki on her bed
statements.evidence: BP 10.3.51: 'devakyāḥ śayane nyasya vasudevo 'tha dārikām.'

statements.claim: He quietly took up again the chains that held him, so that nothing would seem to have changed
statements.evidence: Pack summary: 'returns to the prison, where he lays her beside Devaki and resumes his chains.'

statements.claim: Yashoda woke with no knowledge of what had happened; she did not realize what had been born to her that night, was never told, and the child would be her son
statements.evidence: BP 10.3.52: 'yaśodā nanda-patnī ca jātaṃ param abudhyata'; Harivamsha 1.59: 'against her knowledge.'

statements.claim: Neither of the two mothers would ever know the exchange
statements.evidence: Consistent with the pack (Yashoda 'did not realize'; Devaki later pleads for the girl as her own child in HV 1.59), though framed as narrative summary.

notes: All claims match BP 10.3.50-52 and HV 1.59.

statements.claim: Nanda had the auspicious benedictions recited for his newborn son and performed the birth-rite in the proper way, with bathing and purification
statements.evidence: BP 10.5.1: 'vācayitvā svastyayanaṃ jāta-karmātmajasya vai'; 10.5.3: 'kālena snāna-śaucābhyāṃ saṃskārais tapasejyayā.'

statements.claim: At the proper time the priests and bards - sutas, magadhas and vandins - recited their verses of blessing
statements.evidence: BP 10.5.4: 'saumaṅgalya-giro viprāḥ sūta-māgadha-vandinaḥ.'

statements.claim: To the priests he gave a great number of adorned cows
statements.evidence: BP 10.5.2: 'dhenūnāṃ niyute prādād viprebhyaḥ samalaṅkṛte' (two hundred thousand adorned cows).

statements.claim: All of Vraja was swept and sprinkled; the doorways, courtyards and inner rooms of the houses were washed clean
statements.evidence: BP 10.5.5: 'vrajaḥ sammṛṣṭa-saṃsikta-dvārājira-gṛhāntaraḥ.'

statements.claim: The cattle - cows, bulls and young calves - were led out smeared with turmeric and oil and decked with cloth and ornaments
statements.evidence: BP 10.5.6-7: 'gāvo vṛṣā vatsatarā haridrā-taila-rūṣitāḥ mahārha-vastrābharaṇa-kañcukoṣṇīṣa-bhūṣitāḥ.'

statements.claim: The cowherd women, hearing that a son had been born to Yashoda, came in a bright procession with fresh kumkum, jeweled earrings and necklaces, garments of many colors and garlands, and blessed the child 'May he live long'
statements.evidence: BP 10.5.8-11: 'gopyaś cākarṇya muditā yaśodāyāḥ sutodbhavam'; 'nava-kuṅkuma-kiñjalka...'; 'sumṛṣṭa-maṇi-kuṇḍala-niṣka-kaṇṭhyaś citrāmbarāḥ... śikhā-cyuta-mālya-varṣāḥ'; 'tā āśiṣaḥ prayuñjānāś ciraṃ pāhīti bālake.'

statements.claim: All manner of instruments sounded through the settlement, for this was a great festival
statements.evidence: BP 10.5.12: 'avādyanta vicitrāṇi vāditrāṇi mahotsave.'

statements.claim: The cowherds, full of joy, sprinkled one another with curd, milk, ghee and water
statements.evidence: BP 10.5.13: 'gopāḥ parasparaṃ hṛṣṭā dadhi-kṣīra-ghṛtāmbubhiḥ.'

statements.claim: Nanda, generous-hearted, gave to everyone who came: clothes, ornaments and cattle, honoring each as was fitting
statements.evidence: BP 10.5.14-15: 'nando mahā-manās tebhyo vāso 'laṅkāra-go-dhanam tais taiḥ kāmair adīnātmā yathocitam apūjayat.'

statements.claim: He congratulated the blessed Rohini
statements.evidence: BP 10.5.16: 'rohiṇī ca mahā-bhāgā nanda-gopābhinanditā.'

statements.claim: It was said afterward that from that day Nanda's Vraja was rich in every way
